source.title: Behaviour Is an Incomplete Measure of Reasoning Development: Cross-surface pre-arrival accessibility and the limits of developmental inference in a recurrent-depth reasoner

record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out behavioral acquisition across a curriculum and pre-arrival answer information with probes, using a recurrent-depth relational task rather than the original grokking setup. It does not reproduce the original overfitting-and-delayed-generalization experiment.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out acquisition costs and pre-arrival measurements that bear on V1 and V2. It does not report training accuracy or vary training-set size. Prior-work results mentioned in Related Work are not recorded as rows. The longitudinal accessibility curve was not run because the eligible population could not support the registered estimand.
record.test_reason: The study's results do not bear on any version. It never reports training accuracy, a train-test gap or training-set size, so its held-out acquisition costs cannot show delayed generalization after memorization (V1). Its probes read future-answer identity from frozen checkpoints on items not yet answered: an inference-time accessibility construct, not a training-time progress measure anticipating a jump. The longitudinal probe curve that could have touched V2 was declared not evaluable. Grokking appears only as a Related Work citation of Nanda et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that the longitudinal accessibility curve is non-identifiable, because probe eligibility is defined by behavioural arrival.
record.recipe_differences: A 30M-parameter recurrent-depth transformer is trained on a closed oracle-defined relational world with a hop-depth curriculum and symbolic or verbal surfaces. This differs from the original modular-arithmetic grokking setup; the study also probes hidden states and does not measure training-set-size effects.
record.method_sensitivity: The bundled training surface changes acquisition trajectories substantially; symbolic and verbal probe locations also yield different accuracies. No registered cross-population effect-size test between surfaces was performed.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a hop-depth curriculum, held-out stage acquisition cost depends strongly on input surface: 70 vs 13,055 epochs at k=3. On the verbal surface a long grind was followed by an 8-epoch k=4 clearance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curriculum stage acquisition in recurrent-depth reasoners shows surface-dependent long plateaus followed by rapid transfer to the next depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Future-answer identity is weakly linearly decodable from hidden state before the model answers correctly, on both surfaces: 0.056 verbal, 0.102 symbolic, vs 0.025 chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Answer information is weakly linearly accessible in hidden state before behavioural arrival.

record.problems: One closed synthetic world and one recurrent-depth architecture class; the two surfaces are separate trained realizations and bundle multiple differences; no training accuracy or training-set-size sweep; probe results are weak and heterogeneous; no cross-population effect-size comparison; accessibility does not show causal use; the longitudinal accessibility trajectory was not evaluable.
record.rows_left_out: The full symbolic staircase through k = 20 is plotted, but exact values beyond the tabulated k ≤ 10 subset are not stated numerically in the text and were not extracted as figure-only rows. The study also discusses earlier literature, whose results are not rows.

untested.parts: All: no training accuracy, no overfitting phase, no train-size variation, no modular arithmetic.
All: no circuit identification, no memorization removal; the longitudinal progress-measure curve was not evaluable.
All; the authors state they do not test whether the realizations learn the same algorithm.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked curriculum stage costs to V1 and probes to V2. Neither measures what those versions name: V1 needs training saturation followed by delayed test accuracy, and V2 needs training-time progress measures anticipating a jump. No verdicts are given. Possibly relevant to a curriculum-plateau or latent-accessibility phenomenon instead.

versions.untested_parts: Training accuracy saturation/overfitting, a train-to-test accuracy gap on the same task and stage, modular arithmetic, and whether delay increases as the training set shrinks.

The study does not identify a generalizing circuit, test removal of memorizing components, or estimate gradual circuit development across training. Its longitudinal probe trajectory was not evaluable; it does not establish that continuous progress measures anticipate a behavioral jump.
Non-algorithmic data, initialization scale, weight norm, and a lazy-to-rich transition.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Weight decay or another low-norm bias, efficiency of circuits, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Whether runs converge to the same algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters; the authors explicitly state that they do not test whether the two realizations learn the same algorithm.
Adaptive-optimizer instability and floating-point or softmax artifacts.

rows.check: 13,055-epoch verbal k=3 cost. Training accuracy during the grind is not reported, so it is not shown to be post-memorization delay. It is a surface contrast, not a V1 measure.

rows.subject: verbal surface realization
rows.operation_detail: Right-censored in-stage cost toward the held-out stage criterion (>0.95 accuracy).
rows.value: at least 6,400 logical epochs; right-censored at the manuscript snapshot
rows.note: The stage had not cleared the criterion at the snapshot. The limitations section reports maximum observed accuracy 0.9133 at final evaluated filename epoch 20,399.
rows.check: Right-censored stage cost (max 0.9133). No training accuracy reported.

rows.subject: verbal surface realization
rows.operation_detail: Tracked held-out four-hop accuracy during the verbal k = 3 grind.
rows.measure: Held-out four-hop accuracy across the grind
rows.value: Took only values 0, 0.025, 0.05 and 0.075; exactly zero in 71.3% of frames; peaked at 3/40; ended at 0/40
rows.note: The authors state it remained at floor against the criterion throughout the k = 3 grind; this is higher-hop transfer during another curriculum stage, not same-stage train/test behavior.
rows.check: Higher-hop held-out transfer at floor during k=3 training. These items are outside the training stage, so this is not a delayed-generalization measure.

rows.subject: verbal surface realization
rows.operation_detail: Tracked held-out five-hop accuracy during the verbal k = 3 grind.
rows.measure: Held-out five-hop accuracy across the grind
rows.value: Took only values 0, 0.025 and 0.05; zero in 93.3% of frames; peaked at 2/40; ended at 0/40
rows.note: The authors state it remained at floor against the criterion throughout the k = 3 grind; this is higher-hop transfer during another curriculum stage, not same-stage train/test behavior.
rows.check: Same as r12, for the five-hop battery.

rows.subject: verbal surface realization
rows.operation_detail: Measured a registered content-sensitive differential against a parse-control baseline and confound boundary.
rows.value: 93.25; clearance of 3.75 over the confound boundary
rows.note: A local internal measurement at near-floor behavioral accuracy; the authors say it is not an estimate of mechanism acquisition or a developmental accessibility curve.
rows.check: Single-frame content differential. The authors say it is not a developmental curve or a mechanism-acquisition estimate, and it is not linked to a later jump.

rows.subject: verbal surface realization
rows.stage_stated: frozen checkpoint at registered pre-answer position
rows.operation_detail: Fit a linear classifier over hidden state before the answer slot on items not yet answered correctly; score held-out folds.
rows.baseline: Uniform chance 0.025; zero-step control 0.024758; population frequency baseline 0.048309
rows.uncertainty: Restricted permutation B = 1000; p = 0.012987; null mean 0.0285; null maximum 0.0658
rows.note: The paper characterizes the accessibility as weak and heterogeneous and explicitly distinguishes accessibility from causal use.
rows.check: Inference-time decodability on a frozen checkpoint, not a continuous training-time progress measure or circuit formation.

rows.subject: symbolic surface realization
rows.stage_stated: frozen checkpoint at primary pre-answer position
rows.operation_detail: Fit a linear classifier over hidden state at the registered final query position before the answer slot; score held-out folds.

conditions.value: primary: final observed query position preceding answer slot

rows.baseline: Uniform chance 0.025; zero-step control 0.04598; population frequency baseline 0.04598
rows.uncertainty: Restricted permutation B = 1000; p = 0.000999; null maximum 0.06394
rows.note: The text says the trained value exceeds the entire permutation null distribution. The zero-step and frequency baselines are reported as distinct references despite being numerically identical.
rows.check: As r15: frozen-checkpoint accessibility, not a progress measure across training.

rows.subject: symbolic surface realization
rows.stage_stated: frozen checkpoint at secondary readout comparator position
rows.operation_detail: Fit a linear classifier over hidden state at the separately registered readout comparator position; score held-out folds.
rows.note: The primary and secondary locations were preregistered separately, each with its own threshold; the text does not give a secondary-position zero-step or frequency baseline.
rows.check: As r15, at the secondary comparator position.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Verbal realization, k = 3 to k = 4 sequence
reader_labels.reason: Held-out k = 3 competence cost 13,055 logical epochs was followed by k = 4 clearance in 8 logical epochs (r2, r4); the higher-hop batteries remained at floor during the k = 3 grind (r12, r13). This supports a delayed held-out acquisition sequence, not the full overfitting claim.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Symbolic versus verbal surfaces and later verbal stages
reader_labels.reason: Acquisition costs vary substantially by surface and stage, including 70 versus 13,055 logical epochs at k = 3 and a right-censored verbal k = 5 stage (r1, r2, r5, r11); the study does not establish a training-set-size rule.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Verbal pre-arrival probe and both registered symbolic positions
reader_labels.reason: Future-answer identity was above the reported controls/null references before behavioral arrival on the verbal surface and at both symbolic probe positions (r15–r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The probe effects are weak and class-heterogeneous, and the study does not establish causal use or a training-time developmental trajectory (r14–r17).
